Incidence of Accidental Deaths in the States, Union Territories and Cities. Table III presents the incidence of accidental deaths in different States, Union Territories and important Cities during 1969 and 1970 along with the percentage variations during 1970 over 1969. It may be observed that, although there has been an overall increase of 6.9% in the incidence of accidental deaths during 1970 over 1969, the different States and Union Territories do not reflect any uniform pattern. The States of Bihar, Haryana, Punjab, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal registered decreases, while all the other States reported increases. The highest increase of 215.3% is noticed in Jammu & Kashmir. The other States which registered marked increases are Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Madhya Pradesh, Orissa, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. The causes of the marked increases or decreases are not uniform e.g. the marked increase in Jammu & Kashmir was mostly in the miscellaneous group and accidents on the roads, the former increasing from 226 during 1969 to 1063 during 1970, while the latter increased from 44 to 102. In Madhya Pradesh, there were significant increases in deaths due to drowning, fire and miscellaneous causes. Deaths by drowning increased from 3198 in 1969 to 3713 during 1970, while death due to fire increased from 1154 to 1640.
